topic: Graphlit Event Clock Agentic RAG Guide 2026: Trajectory-Based Context for Tool-Using Agents

competitors.title: Building the Event Clock
key_points: Introduces the 'two clocks' metaphor: state clock (what's true now) vs event clock (what happened, in what order, with what reasoning)
Extends the framing beyond time to a multi-dimensional index: timeline, geospatial, full-text, vector embeddings, graph relationships
Proposes three-layer architecture: Content (immutable evidence), Entities (identity resolution), Facts (temporal assertions with validity periods)
Facts as first-class data with text, validAt, invalidAt, status (Canonical/Superseded/Corroborated/Synthesized), mentions, and source content
Synthesized facts derived from multiple sources enable timeline reasoning and world models without continual learning
Agents need a pre-built map (operational context) before they can walk it effectively — bootstrapping order matters
Dynamic tool discovery pattern: MCP server exposes 3 meta-tools (search_tools, describe_tools, execute_tool) instead of 20+ individual tools
Graphlit shipping Facts mode in Studio Q1 2026, with fact extraction, entity mentions, graph visualization, and LLM-powered fact resolution on roadmap

competitors.title: AI Agent Memory Frameworks in 2026: Memory vs. Context
key_points: Memory and context are different layers: memory is durable persistence, context is the selected working set shown to the model

Five shifts since 2025: chat history no longer enough, temporal memory became central, self-editing memory became table stakes, benchmarks moved past simple recall, context engineering became the product
Comprehensive taxonomy of 8 memory types: working, session, semantic, episodic, entity, procedural, temporal graph, operational context graph
Survey of 11 frameworks: Mem0, Supermemory, Membase, Memory Store, Zep/Graphiti, LangMem, Cognee, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, Anthropic/OpenAI, Graphlit
Recommended architecture: separate agent runtime (task planning, tool selection, reasoning) from context layer (source connectors, entity resolution, temporal facts, permissions)
Five questions to choose a memory layer: personal/agentic/operational?, does time matter?, does provenance matter?, does access control matter?, feature or infrastructure?
Graphlit positioned as context platform underneath agents — ingests 30+ sources, processes through workflows, extracts entities and observations

competitors.title: The Context Layer AI Agents Actually Need
key_points: Two distinct layers: operational context (identity resolution, ownership, temporal state, cross-system synthesis) and decision context (traces, precedent, auditability)
Operational context is the foundation — you can't capture meaningful decision traces without knowing who the actors are and how entities relate
RAG retrieves text chunks, not organizational understanding; AI memory platforms store chat transcripts, not organizational reality
Organizational knowledge is a graph: people connected to accounts, accounts to projects, projects to decisions, all evolving over time
Core capabilities needed: identity-resolved entities, multimodal ingestion, temporal modeling, relationship mapping, agent interoperability, enterprise deployment
Graphlit's 2026 roadmap: CRM as entity spine, agent memory and decision logging, workflow instrumentation
Decision traces need industry standards (like OpenTelemetry for observability) — Graphlit uses Schema.org and JSON-LD

competitors.title: Context Graphs, Honestly
key_points: Response to Forrester's Charles Betz who argued context graphs are a convergence of 40 years of work, not an invention
Agrees with Betz on convergence, fidelity risk, and decision capture as the actual frontier
Disagrees on incumbents winning: the data incumbents hold (IT assets, service tickets) isn't the data that matters for AI agents
Matt Brown's 'Your Data Model Is Your Destiny' framework: the data model is the moat, and incumbents' data models lock them into their original shape
Four-layer data model: Content (immutable evidence), Entities (identity layer), Facts (temporal assertions), Conversations (connective tissue)
Real-world scenario showing why context graphs need to span email, meetings, Slack, CRM, support tickets, and prior agent runs
Fidelity curve looks different when graph is derived from ingested reality instead of typed into forms — CMDB rot pattern doesn't apply
The 'dark matter' of organizational reasoning (phone calls, meetings, hallway conversations) is exactly the substrate context graphs must capture

competitors.title: The Agent Is the User
key_points: Three shapes hiding under 'company brain': orchestration platforms (shape 1), AI-native apps (shape 2), actual context graphs (shape 3)
Shape 3 (context graph) is the only one where the product IS the data layer — typed entity model, multi-source connectors, multimodal indexing, MCP integration
Four primitives of a real context graph: typed entity/relationship model, multi-source live connectors with permissions, multimodal indexing that actually runs, MCP as integration path
Four data layers: Content (immutable evidence), Entities (identity), Facts (temporal assertions), Conversations (connective tissue)
Everything-app graveyard is large — switching costs stack, network effects protect incumbents
The most successful everything-apps (ClickUp, Notion, Atlassian) are spending AI budgets reaching outside their own walls — building context layer features
A file/block/page is for a person; the agent's primitive is the context graph — typed, temporal, multimodal, permission-aware, with conversation history
Shape 3 is the youngest market with cleanest TAM logic — every team has >1 source of truth, every agent needs to act across them

competitors.title: Context Graphs: AI's Trillion-Dollar Opportunity
key_points: The wall isn't missing data — it's missing decision traces: exception logic in people's heads, precedent from past decisions, cross-system synthesis, approval chains outside systems
Context graph as the enduring layer: entities connected by decision events and 'why' links, making precedent searchable
Feedback loop: captured decision traces become searchable precedent, every automated decision adds another trace
Incumbents can't build context graphs: Salesforce built on current state storage, warehouses are in read path not write path
Systems of agents startups have structural advantage: they're in the orchestration path and can capture context at decision time
Three paths for startups: replace entire systems of record, replace modules, or create entirely new systems of record for decision traces
Key signals: high headcount workflows, exception-heavy decisions, organizations at intersection of systems (RevOps, DevOps, Security Ops)

Context graphs as organizational memory that compounds: captured decision traces become searchable precedent, every automated decision adds another trace

Synthesized facts and world models without continual learning: how fact resolution enables static models to behave as if they're learning through expanding evidence bases
